key_findings: The registry is two parallel tables keyed by the same CapabilityDeclarationId: a pure static table (src/composition/capabilityDeclarations.ts:116-530, ~67 keys) mapping capability -> [{identity, operations}], and a runtime table (src/composition/capabilityServices.ts:225-590) mapping the same keys to typed factories; the runtime table is `satisfies Partial<Record<CapabilityDeclarationId,...>>` and createCapabilityServices throws `Undeclared capability <id>` at host construction if a key lacks a declaration (capabilityServices.ts:615-617).

Operations in a declaration are either an explicit list type-checked against TOOL_CONTRACTS names or a `{ group: ToolContractGroupId }` reference into TOOL_CONTRACT_GROUPS (src/contracts/toolFamilies.ts:52-100), so whole groups grow automatically while provider subsets stay explicit (capabilityDeclarations.ts:95-108); the same provider identity may appear under several capabilities (e.g. PWNTOOLS at :193 and :446).

Provider identity is a frozen {id, name, version|null} owned by the adapter module (src/frida/FridaProviderIdentity.ts; src/ghidra/GhidraProviderMetadata.ts:6-10) and imported by both the implementation and the static declaration; the declaration file imports only identity metadata, never factories/schemas/catalogs (capabilityDeclarations.ts:1,115).

Each runtime entry binds construction, close, ownership ('host'|'caller') and availability facts once via `capability(create, close, observe?, ownership?)` / `service(create, observe?)` combinators (capabilityServices.ts:181-210); every service is injectable through CapabilityServiceOptions (:114-149) and ownership is inferred from injection (`outsideHost`, :212-213).

CapabilityScope (src/application/CapabilityScope.ts) is the single lifetime owner: own() rejects duplicate ids and post-shutdown registration; close() joins concurrent closers, removes released peers, retains failed peers for retry and throws AggregateError; caller-owned instances (optionalObservationProviderOwner: 'caller', set in src/main/transport.ts:152) are returned unwrapped and closed by process-level code.

Availability is split into static facts (hostUnsupported, *Enabled booleans derived from platform/arch and isAbsolute(env.REA_*) at construction, no probing) and named live probes `(signal) => Promise<ProviderAvailability>` run only by session discovery and only for advertised tool families (src/application/CapabilityAvailability.ts:6-50; src/server/registerSessionStatusTool.ts:40-78); ProviderAvailability separates `reason` from `remediation` with a stable rejection-code enum (src/domain/providerSelection.ts:19-33).

AnalysisProviderRegistry (src/application/binary/AnalysisProviderRegistry.ts) is deterministic with no fallback: providers sorted by id (:168-172), capability provenance must equal provider identity (:148-157), explicit selector binds exactly that provider or returns a coded rejection (#selectConcrete :572-643), 'auto' evaluates all available+supported candidates in parallel and binds only when exactly one is usable, else `ambiguous` error (>1) or an intentionally unbound route (0) (#selectAutomatically :645-744).

SessionProviderRouter.selectable asserts unique provider ids and that auxiliary operation sets are disjoint from each other and from deep declared operations (SessionProviderRouter.ts:45-66,203-227); it yields one immutable SessionProviderRoute per target transition and wraps multiple providers in CompositeProvider, which routes operation->provider and creates child clients lazily (CompositeProvider.ts:129-284).

BinarySession owns the single active target shared by CLI and MCP; target transitions are serialized behind a drain barrier (#transition/#transitionGeneration/#transitionPending, BinarySession.ts:191-193), open runs `health` before committing the new binding and restores the previous target on failure (:553-700); src/composition/binary.ts:23-27 is 'the sole production wiring point' for deep candidates (Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, Kuna) plus LazyAnalysisProvider auxiliaries.

Optional observation providers (browser, browser scenario, Electron, Electron active, V8 inspector) load independently via dynamic import(); each failure is captured as {providerId, reason} instead of failing startup and surfaces at tool-call time as AnalysisCapabilityUnavailableError('Adapter could not load: ...') (src/composition/optionalObservationProviders.ts:66-122; src/application/OptionalObservationProviders.ts:37-46); auxiliary providers expose static identity+capabilities and defer implementation load to first execute (LazyAnalysisProvider.ts:46-67, src/providers/DeferredAnalysisClient.ts).

Every public tool is a ToolContract {name, title, description, kind, inputSchema (zod), outputSchema, effects, annotations, returnsTargetContent, examples} (src/contracts/toolContractTypes.ts:37-67); TOOL_EFFECTS is a mandatory per-tool audit (toolContractMetadata throws 'Missing effect audit', toolEffects.ts:819-831), MCP hints are derived from effects with executesForeignCode||mutatesDevice => destructive (:765-787), and any tool not in TARGET_CONTENT_FREE_TOOLS is marked as returning untrusted target content (:800-816).

Tool families: TOOL_FAMILY_DEFINITIONS (toolFamilies.ts:116-245, 18 families) must cover every contract exactly once (toolFamilies.test.ts:64-73); registerToolFamilies requires a complete map typed by ToolFamilyId (toolFamilyIds.ts:41-45) so adding a family id is a compile error at createServer.ts:347 and the CLI until registrars exist; toolRegistrationOptions projects the Zod contract directly into SDK registration (src/server/toolRegistrationOptions.ts:13-47).

Catalog pipeline (package.json:327): tsc -> record-catalog-digests.mjs (sha256 over canonical JSON of 6 schema profiles into dist/recordedCatalogDigests.js) -> record-mcp-catalog.mjs (boots a real server over InMemoryTransport under an isolated HOME, writes dist/mcp-catalog*.json + hashes; deferredRuntime.ts:25-47 refuses to start on hash mismatch) -> bundle; generate-product-catalog.mjs projects docs/public/product-catalog.json from compiled dist modules including dist/composition/capabilityDeclarations.js (scripts/lib/catalog-core.mjs:35-44).

Catalog validation: providerCatalog throws on conflicting identity, unknown contract group, or unknown operation (scripts/lib/catalog-builders.mjs:40-64); toolFamilyCatalog asserts family total == TOOL_CONTRACTS.length == FULL_CATALOG_IDENTITY.counts.mcp_tools (:17-22); `--check` mode fails on 'missing or stale' without rewriting; tests/boundary/filesystem/productCatalog.test.ts:74-124 compares the committed JSON to a fresh projection and runs documentation-fact checks; generate-mcp-tool-catalog.mjs validates every advertised JSON Schema with Ajv2020; scripts/lint/rules/tool-catalog-sources.mjs walks TOOL_CONTRACTS spreads by AST only.

Dependency direction (AGENTS.md:17; docs/architecture.mermaid) is enforced by scripts/lib/module-boundaries.mjs (run from `npm run lint`, package.json:145,309): domain/contracts may import only domain/contracts ('pure-layer', :71-77), application may not import composition (:78-79), application/server may not import provider roots or the centralised Frida/Cutter/GDB/Rizin constructors except as type-only imports (:27-28,80-94); docs/capability-composition.md:29-34 explains this is what lets CLI one-shot adapters import a single factory while MCP materialises the whole host.

docs/capability-composition.md:27 and :102-103 state REA has 'no generic JSON operation dispatcher' and that 'External plugin distribution, automatic provider installation and a universal provider interface are separate concerns'; the composition is an internal, hand-wired contract (createServer.ts:347 registrar map; binary.ts:83 deep candidate array), which is the central tension with a runtime-pluggable 'universal tool registry'.
extensibility_points: Static/runtime split: capabilityDeclarations.ts (pure, importable by generators and discovery without loading schemas or engines) vs capabilityServices.ts (factories with close/ownership/availability), cross-checked by `satisfies` at compile time and by the `Undeclared capability` throw at host construction.

Contract-group references ({ group: ToolContractGroupId }) instead of copied operation lists, so a provider bound to a group inherits new group operations automatically; explicit subsets remain available for partial providers.

Adapter-owned frozen ProviderIdentity constants imported by both the provider implementation and the static declaration; the registry rejects provenance mismatch (AnalysisProviderRegistry.ts:148-157) and the catalog builder rejects conflicting identities (catalog-builders.mjs:40-46).

`capability()` / `service()` combinators that bind construction, cleanup, ownership and availability in one entry; CapabilityScope as the sole close-owner with retry-on-failure semantics; no separate provider-close list to maintain.

CapabilityServiceOptions makes every service/port injectable; ownership ('host' vs 'caller') is derived from whether a value was injected, which is how SDK-created server instances borrow process-owned optional observation ports.

Availability facts as data (hostUnsupported, *Enabled) plus named AbortSignal-taking probes, merged by the host and consumed only by discovery for advertised families; constructors never probe or launch.

Lazy/deferred provider pattern: LazyAnalysisProvider + DeferredAnalysisClient expose static identity and capability descriptors synchronously and import the implementation on first execute; optional factories use dynamic import() with per-port failure capture.

Deterministic, order-independent composition: sorted provider ids and operations, composite identity `composite:a+b`, 'Registration order never affects selection', 'catalog order never selects a handler or schema'; disjoint-operation assertions in SessionProviderRouter/CompositeProvider.

Typed family registrar map (registerToolFamilies with {[Id in ToolFamilyId]: () => void}) so a new family id forces both CLI and MCP call sites to be updated at compile time; TOOL_FAMILY_IDS lives in a schema-free module for cheap startup validation.
Per-tool TOOL_EFFECTS audit table with derived MCP annotations and an untrusted-by-default returnsTargetContent allowlist; toolContractMetadata throws if a tool lacks an audit.

Generated, digest-verified catalogs (product catalog, recorded MCP catalog, catalog digest profiles) projected from compiled code and validated in --check mode and by tests; deferred runtime refuses to start on hash mismatch.
Mechanically enforced dependency direction (module-boundaries.mjs) with explicit type-only exceptions for centralised constructors, making application workflows reusable across CLI and MCP adapters.
relevance_to_control_plane: Borrow the two-table design: a pure 'target/driver capability declaration' (which operations a driver can perform on which app, with stable driver identity) separate from runtime driver bindings, keyed identically and cross-checked at compile time and host construction; generate the agent-facing catalog from the static table so docs cannot drift from code.

Borrow CapabilityScope semantics verbatim for driver lifetimes (accessibility connections, CDP sessions, injected agents, OS automation handles): single owner, duplicate-id refusal, sealed after shutdown, joined concurrent closes, failed closers retained for retry, aggregated errors.

Borrow the availability model: side-effect-free static facts (platform, permission grants, configured absolute paths) plus named live probes with AbortSignal run only at discovery for advertised families; return ProviderAvailability-style {status, code, reason, remediation, diagnostics} so the agent gets actionable unavailability instead of a stack trace.

Borrow the mandatory per-tool effects audit and derived annotations; a drive-capable plane should keep REA's rule that executesForeignCode/mutatesDevice are destructive by definition and add the provider-level CapabilityEffects fields that already exist (mayShowUi, changesPermissions, requiresRoot); treat all target-derived text (UI labels, window titles, clipboard, screen OCR) as untrusted unless audited, since it is a prompt-injection channel.

Borrow independent optional loading with captured {providerId, reason} failures surfaced at call time, and lazy providers whose identity/capabilities are static so discovery never loads heavy driver code (Frida bindings, Playwright, platform accessibility libraries).

Borrow deterministic no-fallback selection with an explicit `ambiguous` error and an 'unbound' route: when several drivers could reach one app (accessibility tree vs CDP vs vision vs Frida), make the choice caller-visible rather than silently picking one; use disjoint-operation routing (SessionProviderRouter/CompositeProvider) when one target is served by several drivers.

Borrow the dependency-direction rule and its mechanical checker (domain/contracts import nothing else; application never imports composition; adapters reach drivers only via ports/factories) so the same workflows serve CLI, MCP and any future HTTP surface.
Borrow digest-verified generated catalogs and the --check/test pattern that compares the committed artifact with a fresh projection.

Avoid lifting REA as a plugin host: it deliberately has no generic operation dispatcher and no external plugin loading (capability-composition.md:27,102-103); a runtime-pluggable 'universal agentic API' trades away the exact-typed contract binding REA relies on. Decide explicitly whether to keep REA-style compile-time registration (fork and add targets in source) or build a runtime plugin boundary with its own validation.
Avoid lifting BinarySession's single-active-target transition barrier unchanged; driving several desktop apps concurrently needs an N-target session model.
Avoid reusing REA's analysis-shaped domain types (Evidence, AnalysisProfile, BinaryTarget) wholesale; the composition patterns transfer, the vocabulary mostly does not.

Adopt REA's own gate as a self-imposed rule: CONTRIBUTING.md:147-153 requires review of target selection, execution and mutation authority, provenance, resource limits, cancellation and cleanup for anything that launches/attaches/injects/changes memory; this is precisely the review a 'drive anything' layer needs, and REA's scope exclusions (DRM/license/anti-cheat/access-control bypass, anti-debugging evasion) mark the boundary the downstream project also states.
constraints_or_risks: Scope/authorization: CONTRIBUTING.md:133-195 and AGENTS.md:7 require explicit maintainer scope decisions before integrating capabilities with target execution, injection, mutation or protection recovery, and exclude DRM/license/anti-cheat/access-control bypass, anti-debugging/anti-instrumentation evasion and attack automation; 'Moving a capability into an optional dependency or plugin does not exempt it.' A general drive layer falls in the category REA says needs this review.

REA's effect audit makes most drive operations destructive by definition (executesForeignCode || mutatesDevice => destructiveHint, toolEffects.ts:779-783); an agent-facing plane must present them that way rather than downgrade them to look safe.
Target content is untrusted by default (TARGET_CONTENT_FREE_TOOLS allowlist); a UI-reading control plane that drops this marker exposes the agent to prompt injection from on-screen text.

The composition is an internal, hand-wired contract (createServer.ts:347 registrar map, binary.ts:83 candidate array), not a plugin API; docs/capability-composition.md:102-103 explicitly places external plugin distribution and a universal provider interface out of scope. Expect to fork/redesign rather than extend in place.

Footprint: ~67 capability keys, ~45 contract groups, 18 families, a 1,022-line registry and 1,681-line session; the verification report records 0.7-1.1 GB kernel peak for single MCP lifecycle tasks with a real Ghidra engine (docs/verification/capability-composition-2026-11-01.md:69-73,98-101). Distill patterns, not breadth.

Static *Enabled facts rely on isAbsolute(env.REA_*_COMMAND) heuristics; a relative command defers to execution-time failure (capabilityServices.ts:151-163), so 'enabled' means 'configured', not 'verified'.

Licensing: LICENSE is MIT; bridged commercial engines (Hopper, IDA, JEB) are bring-your-own (AGENTS.md:11). UNKNOWN whether any third_party/ submodule carries terms affecting a derived distribution; not inspected in this area.

Supply chain (noted, not evaluated): server.json advertises runtimeHint 'npx' for rea-agents over stdio; the deferred runtime hash-verifies its recorded catalog but that protects catalog integrity, not package provenance.

Two effect vocabularies coexist (contract-level ToolEffects vs provider-descriptor CapabilityEffects with mayShowUi/changesPermissions/requiresRoot); no reconciliation point was found, so a distilled design should pick one or define the mapping.
open_questions: How exactly do CLI one-shot commands import 'the selected factory' without the full host (capability-composition.md:31-32)? src/composition/directAnalysis.ts binds sessions lazily, but not every CLI command's factory path was traced.

Is there any completeness check in the inverse direction (every CAPABILITY_DECLARATIONS key has a registered MCP tool/CLI command)? The catalog builder validates operations against TOOL_CONTRACTS, but no declaration->registration test was found.
artifactResources: { providers: [] } is the only capability with no provenance; is this a one-off shared-scope special case or a pattern for future runtime-only capabilities?

The verification report cites issue #8429 and epic #740 for the composition increment; what further composition steps (e.g. a plugin boundary) are planned? docs/roadmap.md exists but was not read for this area.
Are CapabilityEffects (provider descriptor) and ToolEffects (contract audit) reconciled anywhere, or can session inventory report a provider effect the contract audit does not?

README.md provider-selection prose was not located by grep ('Choosing a deep analysis provider', 'REA_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER', 'ambiguous' returned nothing); the selection semantics in the report are from source only.
